subject.title: [Bug]: codex/* provider POSTs to legacy /backend-api/responses (403) at clean boot while sibling openai/* canonicalizes to /backend-api/codex/responses (200) — 2026.7.1

question: Which owner boundary should be responsible for canonicalizing the ChatGPT OAuth Responses endpoint: OpenClaw's Codex plugin/catalog or the sibling Codex app-server contract?
rationale: The proposed shared OpenAI normalization is only safe if current main proves that OpenClaw owns the endpoint construction rather than forwarding an app-server-owned transport configuration.

options.title: Verify and fix at the owning boundary
options.body: Trace the live clean-boot configuration into the Codex runtime, then make one focused fix and regression test at the layer that creates the endpoint.

options.title: Close as external-runtime behavior
options.body: If current OpenClaw forwards the documented Codex endpoint unchanged and the legacy URL originates inside Codex, route the report upstream with the captured OpenClaw configuration evidence.

recommendation.title: Verify and fix at the owning boundary
recommendation.body: Trace the live clean-boot configuration into the Codex runtime, then make one focused fix and regression test at the layer that creates the endpoint.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior work is the closest available history signal for Codex OAuth request construction, although ownership remains low-confidence.
